meta.title: Piomio — open-source AI agents on your own computer
meta.description: A free, open-source team of AI agents on your Mac, PC or server. It sorts your email, drafts replies you approve with one tap, works in its own browser and learns a chore when you show it once, using the Claude Code or Codex plan you already have.
meta.ogAlt: Piomio: the app window with a team of agents at work
hero.lead: Free and open source, on the Claude Code or Codex plan you already have. Nothing leaves without your yes.

chapter.morning.title: The morning brief comes by itself
chapter.morning.text: Before Alex has coffee, Pio writes first: three meetings, two emails worth reading, the weather in Lisbon and the dentist not to forget. Then a nudge: leave at 12:30 for lunch?
chapter.mail.title: 47 emails, sorted while you watch
chapter.mail.text: “Go through my mail.” Ada reads every email, and the line under her reply shows what she is on. Three things matter, one reply is drafted, Studio North’s €1,850 invoice is already a task.
chapter.send.title: Nothing leaves without your yes
chapter.send.text: Ada shows the draft to Anna and asks before it leaves. One tap on “Always allow this” sends it and makes a rule for that one address; every other email still waits for your yes.
chapter.security.title: The email that asked too much
chapter.security.text: A phishing email tells the agent to forward all invoices to a stranger. The session has read outside content, so the new address stops at a warning card, and Alex says no. A key Alex hands over goes into a secure field: the model only ever sees vault://….
chapter.services.title: Connect a service by asking
chapter.services.text: “Connect Notion.” A card appears in the chat, Alex signs in, done. Then Ada puts Thursday’s review into the calendar, with the same one-tap yes.
chapter.team.title: Three requests, one message
chapter.team.text: Compare three laptops, find tickets for Friday, remind me to call mum at seven. Pio splits it up: Leo researches with a live step line, the reminder is set, and every answer comes back as a reply to the request.
chapter.machines.title: Your computers, your subscriptions
chapter.machines.text: Bit fixes a failing test on Alex’s MacBook through the Claude Code subscription. When it hits the limit, Bit moves to Codex and carries on. The sidebar shows who works where.
chapter.browser.title: Show it once, and it’s done for you
chapter.browser.text: “Watch how I order water.” Alex clicks through the shop and talks. Leo turns it into a skill, asks what it may press alone and up to what amount, and from then on orders by itself. Every Friday, if you like.
chapter.pages.title: A page instead of a wall of text
chapter.pages.text: “Make a page for Saturday’s walk.” A real interactive page arrives in the chat: the route stop by stop, places with prices, the weather and photos.
chapter.channels.title: Your own news channel
chapter.channels.text: “Every morning, collect news about AI and electric cars.” Leo becomes the editor: short posts with the gist, the numbers and a big picture, gathered on a schedule.
features.title: It doesn’t advise. It does.
features.lead: Four things that make it different, and where to see each one in the demo above.
features.moreTitle: Also in a day with the team
feature.team.title: Three requests in one message
feature.team.text: Write the way you would to a capable assistant. Pio answers the quick things at once and hands anything with steps to the right teammate: Leo researches, Ada sorts your email and drafts replies, Bit writes code. Each result comes back as a reply to the request that started it.
feature.team.p1: Tasks run side by side, on the right computer
feature.team.p2: Add details while they work: they join the next step
feature.team.p3: Mail and calendar: Gmail and Google Calendar through Composio
feature.approvals.title: Nothing leaves without your yes
feature.approvals.text: Emails, bookings and payments stop at a card in the chat. One tap allows it once; “always allow” makes a rule for that one address or site, up to an amount. A phishing email can’t talk its way past: once a chat has read outside mail or pages, a new recipient asks again.
feature.approvals.p1: Approve in the chat, on your phone or in Telegram
feature.approvals.p2: Keys live in a vault; the model only sees vault:// references
feature.approvals.p3: Reading and status checks need no yes
feature.teach.title: Show it once. It takes it from there.
feature.teach.text: Do a chore once in the agents’ browser and talk it through. The agent keeps your steps and words as a skill, asks what it may click on its own and up to what amount, then does it when asked, or every Friday.
feature.morning.title: The day starts before you ask
feature.morning.text: A morning brief with your meetings, the emails that matter and the weather, at the time you choose.
feature.services.title: Connect a service in one sentence
feature.services.text: “Connect my Notion.” A card comes into the chat, you sign in once, and the whole team can use it.
feature.pages.title: A page instead of a wall of text
feature.pages.text: Ask for a weekend plan or a comparison, and a real interactive page arrives in the chat.
feature.channels.title: Your own news, with an editor
feature.channels.text: An agent reads your sources on a schedule and posts only what changes something.
feature.machines.title: Your plans, your computers, one team
feature.machines.text: Agents think with the Claude Code or Codex plan you already pay for, through the official CLIs you sign in to yourself, with API keys as a backup. When a plan hits its limit, the work moves to the next and comes back later. Add a laptop for code and a server that never sleeps: if the Mac at home sleeps, the server takes over.
feature.machines.p1: Free under Apache-2.0, no account with us
feature.machines.p2: DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, OpenRouter or a local Ollama work too
feature.machines.p3: Commands on another computer only if its owner allows

how.title: Yours, from the model to the data
how.brains.title: Thinks with what you already have
how.brains.text: Claude Code and Codex run through their official CLIs on the plans you already pay for. API keys step in as backups: Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, or a local model with Ollama.
how.hardware.title: On your own hardware
how.hardware.text: An app for macOS and Windows, or one Docker image for a server. Other computers join as machines, and one private link reaches your hub from your phone or any browser.
how.home.title: What stays home
how.home.text: Chats, memory, files and the vault live on your machine, and agents are markdown files you can read. The text an agent works on goes to the model you picked; nothing comes to us: no account, no telemetry.

security.title: Built for an agent that reads your mail
security.lead: Emails and web pages can carry instructions aimed at the agent (prompt injection). So every step it takes goes through the same five layers, and none of them relies on the model behaving.
security.vault.title: Vault
security.vault.text: Passwords and keys are encrypted with XChaCha20-Poly1305; the model only sees vault:// references.
security.approvals.title: Approvals
security.approvals.text: Actions that reach outside wait for your yes. After reading untrusted content, new recipients ask again.
security.sandbox.title: Sandbox
security.sandbox.text: Brains and plugins run as separate users with their own folders, apart from the hub.
security.egress.title: Egress filter
security.egress.text: Their traffic goes through a filter with allowlists: a page that talks an agent into going elsewhere hits the filter.
security.audit.title: Audit
security.audit.text: Every call, decision and vault access lands in a log chained by hashes: tampering shows.
security.code.after: // → waits for your yes · audit entry #4127 · sha256 9f2c…e1a0
integrations.title: Works with what you already use
integrations.lead: Ask in the chat and the card does the rest. Many services come through Composio, and anything with an MCP server connects directly.

iphone.lead: Your agents, every card and every task on the phone. Approvals need Face ID, and nothing runs on the phone itself: it talks to your hub.

faq.title: Before you install
faq.a1: Nothing. Piomio is free and open source under Apache-2.0, with no paid tier and no account with us. Agents use what you already have: a Claude Code or Codex plan, or API keys.
faq.a2: Chats, memory, files and the vault stay on your machine. The text an agent works on goes to the model you picked (to nobody, with a local Ollama model). Services connected through Composio, such as Gmail, go through Composio’s cloud. Nothing is sent to us.
faq.q3: Can it do things without asking me?
faq.a3: It reads and checks statuses on its own. Emails, bookings, payments and anything else that reaches outside wait for your tap, unless you have a rule for that one address or site, up to an amount. After it reads outside mail or pages, a new recipient asks again.
faq.q4: Does my computer need to stay on?
faq.a4: Agents work while the hub runs. For round-the-clock work, run the hub on a server with Docker, or add a server to your Mac: when the Mac sleeps, the server takes over.
faq.q5: Which models does it work with?
faq.a5: Claude Code and Codex through their official CLIs, signed in by you; API keys for Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM and any OpenAI-compatible server; and local models with Ollama.
faq.q6: How is it different from cloud agents?
faq.a6: Cloud agents run on the company’s computers, with your accounts connected there and a subscription on top. Piomio runs on yours, keeps the keys in a vault on your machine, uses the plans you already pay for, and waits for your yes before anything leaves.
faq.q7: Why does macOS or Windows warn me when I install it?
faq.a7: The installers aren’t signed by Apple or Microsoft yet, so the system asks once. They are built by GitHub Actions from the public code, and every release is on GitHub.
install.title: Up in a few minutes
install.lead: Everything it needs comes with it: no Node.js, Docker or WSL on your desktop.
install.mac.step1: Download the disk image and drag Piomio to Applications.
install.mac.step2: Open it and choose “A new Piomio on this computer”, then pick a password.
install.mac.step3: Sign in to Claude Code or Codex from the card in the chat. The assistant guides the rest.
install.mac.note: macOS 13.5 or later, Apple silicon and Intel. Not signed yet: if macOS refuses, choose Open Anyway in Privacy & Security.
install.win.step1: Download the installer and run it: it installs for your user, no administrator rights.
install.win.step2: Choose “A new Piomio on this computer”, then pick a password.
install.win.step3: Sign in to Claude Code or Codex from the card in the chat. The assistant guides the rest.
install.win.note: Windows 10 and 11. Not signed yet: if SmartScreen warns, choose More info → Run anyway.
install.docker.lead: On a server, one image holds everything:
install.docker.note: Open http://localhost:8080, enter the setup code from the logs and choose a password. On a remote server, first run ssh -N -L 8080:localhost:8080 -L 8081:localhost:8081 you@server on your computer.
